summary: POC scoping call to decide which deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private) fits Acme's latency, cost, and security requirements. Agreed to run benchmarks against their workload and scope a 4-week pilot for hosted+Dedicates trial with option to evaluate private if needed.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Rachel Nguyen (Acme CTO), Daniel Park (Platform Eng), Maya Singh (Security), Ethan Li (ML Eng)

Summary (auto): quick intro, collect success criteria, discuss workload numbers, propose benchmark plan, and align on timeline and next steps.

[00:00] Sofia (Redwood - AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro from our side, im sofia, ae, and liam se will go into the technical details, priya will be your csm. how are you all?
[00:20] Rachel (Acme - CTO): good thanks, we, uh, appreciate you taking the time. we want to scope a POC for our chat and search features, main goals are performance and data isolation concerns.
[00:36] Liam (Redwood - SE): awesome, rachel. quick agenda: success criteria, traffic profile, baseline benchmarks, then deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and finally next steps. sound good?
[00:48] Daniel (Acme - Platform Eng): yep perfect.

[02:10] Sofia: before we dive in, can you share top success criteria? like latency targets, cost, and security TODOs?
[02:20] Rachel: yeah. for chat we need p95 under 250ms ideally but p99 under 500ms is okay for our interactive product. for embeddings/search, throughput matters more, we do batch embeddings overnight but also some real-time scoring at ~200 qps. data residency: customer data must remain in our VPC and be encrypted at rest. SOC 2 required, plus SSO integration.

[04:05] Maya (Acme - Security): and clarify - we need KMS/HSM integration for keys and audit logs retained for 12 months. also RBAC and SAML SSO.

[05:30] Liam: got it. those are pretty standard. quick thing on latency: our hosted API usually gives lowest setup friction but you trade off hard isolation; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower variance, Private gives full control for KMS and air-gapped needs.

[06:10] Ethan (Acme - ML Eng): what's the difference for GPU types? like will dedicated use different instance types?
[06:22] Liam: yes, in dedicated you reserve GPU pools — typically A100 or H100 equivalent depending on model; for hosted we auto-select. on private you manage the infra or we ship a validated package. sometimes we see a 10-30% perf delta depending on kernels and sequence lengths.

[08:00] Daniel: for our workload, average message length 120 tokens, peak concurrent users ~3k which maps to roughly 150 qps for chat, but embeddings real-time scoring spikes to 200 qps as rachel said. daily token volume approx 20M tokens.

[09:15] Sofia: ok that helps. for cost modeling we need tokens per month + peak QPS. we can run a benchmark with your sample traffic and measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput.

[10:40] Rachel: timeline wise we want a pilot in March, decision by end of April. ideally 4-6 week POC.

[12:00] Liam: proposed POC plan: week 1 - baseline integration + small synthetic tests; week 2 - run customer traffic replay; week 3 - stress tests and Failover scenarios; week 4 - security review and wrap up. if we find we need private, add provisioning lead time ~6-8 weeks for on-prem or VPC private deployment.

[14:30] Maya: provisioning lead time is critical for us, if private is needed we need procurement windows and security review aligned. can you share SOC 2 and architecture diagrams?
[14:45] Priya (Redwood - CSM): yes we'll share SOC 2 and the security playbook. also a preflight checklist for VPC peering.

[16:20] Daniel: back to benchmarks — what metrics do you capture? p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimate per token? and KV cache hit rate?
[16:34] Liam: exactly. p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/sec / requests/sec), GPU utilization, and for serving we track KV cache efficiency (we sometimes call it k v cache in docs) and batching stats. cost modeling includes batch efficiency and quantization impact.

[18:00] Ethan: about quantization - will that change output quality? we have some sensitive scoring tests, can't tolerate quality regressions.
[18:12] Liam: good call; we recommend A/B evals against your prompt set. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles but we keep quality gated; if quality regress we rollback. we usually run automatic evals on a holdout prompt set.

[20:15] Rachel: security question - can hosted API do bring-your-own-key?
[20:23] Sofia: hosted supports envelope encryption, and we integrate with customer KMS in dedicated/private more directly. hosted BYOK has constraints — we can discuss specifics in security doc.

[22:00] Maya: also need assurance on logs and retention. we require audit logs pushed to our SIEM or S3.
[22:08] Priya: we support audit exports, and for private we can ship logs to your collector; for dedicated we have options. we'll include the retention table.

[24:00] Daniel: cost — you mentioned target of $0.0008 per token. how do we get there?
[24:10] Liam: that'll depend on batching, cache, and quantization. Dedicated with reserved capacity plus batch tuning often gives the best unit economics for steady workloads. hosted is easier to start but might be higher per-token. private could be best if you already own infra but has upfront ops cost.

[26:40] Rachel: for decision criteria let's list them: 1) latency and variance, 2) predictable cost, 3) data residency/isolation, 4) time-to-prod and ops overhead, 5) compliance requirements.

[27:10] Sofia: exactly. quick mapping: Hosted = fastest time to value, good for eval and early ramp; Dedicated = best for steady predictable throughput and cost; Private = necessary if strict data residency/KMS/HSM or air-gapped needs.

[29:30] Ethan: any limitations on model support across modes? like model variants or quantization?
[29:40] Liam: some bleeding-edge quant kernels may be limited on hosted while we vet; Dedicated we can pin kernel versions and compiler flags; private is most flexible but you manage the infra. sometimes proprietary kernels for H100 are gated.

[32:00] Rachel: for the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[32:08] Liam: sample traffic capture (we prefer a 24h sample with timestamps), example prompts, expected concurrency curve, and any SSO/KMS test accounts. also indicate which models you want to test (open model names).

[33:20] Daniel: we can provide a sanitized 24h trace, and an infra endpoint for replay. note: traffic has bursts during promo windows where QPS spikes 3x for ~15 minutes.

[34:15] Sofia: we'll include spike tests in stress week. will also run a prefix cache test to measure KV hit rate benefits.

[36:00] Maya: can we get an NDA addendum for the benchmark data?
[36:10] Priya: yes, we'll send an addendum.

[37:40] Liam: regarding SLOs, what uptime SLA do you expect?
[37:47] Rachel: 99.9% is our baseline for production, plus error budget alerts.

[38:20] Liam: Dedicated supports SLA-backed uptime, hosted has tiered SLAs, private depends on your ops. we'll document options.

[40:00] Sofia: ok let's talk timelines again - you mentioned decision by end of April. we can start the POC in the first week of March if you sign the SOW. estimated 4 weeks of active work, then a review. if private is required we'll surface costs and lead time asap.

[42:30] Daniel: who will run the benchmarks? do we want Redwood to run them against your hosted infra, or run them in our env?
[42:40] Liam: both — we prefer a dual-run: Redwood-run on hosted and dedicated to compare, and a customer-run replay in your environment to check network egress and VPC latency. that gives apples-to-apples.

[44:10] Ethan: for the customer-run, do you provide a test harness?
[44:15] Liam: yes, we'll provide a test harness and the benchmark plan. we'll instrument with our tracing to capture token-level latencies.

[46:00] Rachel: any deal-breakers we should worry about?
[46:06] Maya: if we can't satisfy the KMS/HSM integration or audit log forwarding, that's a blocker. also any inability to guarantee data doesn't persist outside our control.

[47:30] Priya: understood. we'll include explicit KMS integration steps and log-forwarding options.

[49:00] Sofia: recap: we will send SOW and POC pricing by 2026-03-02. Redwood will prepare benchmark plan + test harness by 2026-03-05. Acme will provide traffic sample, SSO/KMS test accounts, and compliance checklist by 2026-03-03. we'll aim to start first week of March. if private is needed, we'll discuss provisioning lead times and procurement.

[51:20] Daniel: sounds good. one more nit — for dedicated, any minimum commitment?
[51:28] Sofia: dedicated typically comes with a reserved monthly commit for capacity to get best pricing; for the POC we can offer a short-term trial bucket to validate perf with limited commit.

[53:10] Rachel: ok, that helps.

[54:00] Liam: i'll add an example benchmark spreadsheet with expected metrics and columns: request id, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, model, kernel, batch_size.

[55:20] Ethan: great. also include a quality column to show any regressions vs baseline.

[56:10] Sofia: perfect. any final questions?
[56:20] Maya: none here.
[56:30] Rachel: no. thanks everyone.

[57:00] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and SOW.

[58:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: some words like "k v cache" or "dedicate" were auto-transcribed incorrectly; occasional overlap and filler words omitted.
